title: Big Night
tagline: One night to save the restaurant.
about: Two Italian brothers bet everything on one huge dinner to save their struggling restaurant.
cue: Bring out the timpano when the dinner party is still waiting on Louis Prima.
faces: The customer who wanted spaghetti too
Primo in the kitchen. Secondo out front.
Seafood risotto. The one the customer wanted spaghetti with
Risotto in three colours. Green, white and red, side by side, at the feast
Timpano. The pasta drum. One bite and the room shouts Paradise
Roast pork, whole-pig style. Part of the feast on the big night
Secondo's omelette. The morning after. Cooked in silence, split three ways
No spaghetti with the risotto. Primo: she is a Philistine.
The long table, the big night
For the night Louis Prima was meant to come. To eat good food is to be close to God.

    StartersMains
    StartersSeafood risottoThe one the customer wanted spaghetti withHow to make it1 L fish stock1 onion, diced2 garlic cloves, chopped3 tbsp olive oil280g carnaroli rice125ml white wine300g green prawns, peeled200g squid rings500g mussels, cleaned30g butter1 bunch parsley1 lemonPeel the prawns, scrub and debeard the mussels, dice the onion, chop the garlic and chop the parsley.Warm the fish stock in a saucepan. Soften the onion and garlic in the olive oil over medium heat for 5 minutes.Add the carnaroli rice and toast for 2 minutes, then pour in the white wine and stir until it is absorbed.Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 16 minutes until the rice is nearly tender.Stir in the prawns, squid rings and mussels, cover and cook for 4 minutes until the mussels open. Throw out any that stay shut.Take off the heat and stir through the butter, the parsley and a squeeze of lemon. Serve straight away, no cheese.Risotto in three coloursGreen, white and red, side by side, at the feastHow to make it1 onion, diced70g butter240g arborio rice125ml white wine850ml chicken stock100g baby spinach1 bunch basil60g parmesan, grated4 tbsp tomato passata1 pinch saffron threadsHeat the chicken stock in a saucepan. Soak the saffron in 2 tbsp of hot water. Blitz the baby spinach and basil leaves with a splash of the stock to a smooth paste.Soften the onion in 40g of the butter for 5 minutes, add the arborio rice and toast for 2 minutes, then add the white wine and stir until absorbed.Add the hot stock a ladle at a time, stirring, for 17 minutes until the rice is just tender.Split the risotto into three pans over low heat. Stir the spinach and basil paste into the first, the parmesan and the last 30g butter into the second, and the passata with the saffron and its water into the third.Spoon the green, white and red risotto side by side on each plate.MainsTimpanoThe pasta drum. One bite and the room shouts ParadiseHow to make it300g 00 flour3 eggs, for dough40g butter, for the bowl500g beef mince1 onion, diced700ml passata400g ziti, cooked100g salami, diced3 eggs, boiled and sliced, for the filling150g provolone, dicedCook 180g dried ziti in well salted water until just tender, then drain.Make a dough with the flour and eggs, knead and rest.Brown the mince with the onion, add the passata and simmer to a ragù.Roll the dough thin and line an ovenproof bowl greased with the butter.Toss the cooked ziti with ragù and layer in the bowl with salami, boiled egg and provolone.Fold the dough over and bake at 180°C for 1 hour.Rest for 30 minutes, turn out and slice.Roast pork, whole-pig stylePart of the feast on the big nightHow to make it1.5kg boned pork belly2 tsp salt1 tbsp fennel seeds4 garlic cloves, crushed1 bunch rosemaryScore the skin of the pork belly with a sharp knife. Turn it over and rub the flesh side with the fennel seeds, crushed garlic and chopped rosemary.Rub the skin with the salt, roll the pork belly up and tie with string every 3cm.Sit it on a rack and dry uncovered in the fridge overnight.Roast at 240°C for 30 minutes until the skin starts to blister.Turn the oven down to 160°C and roast for 2 hours until tender with crisp crackling.Rest for 15 minutes, cut off the string and carve thick.Secondo's omeletteThe morning after. Cooked in silence, split three waysHow to make it8 eggssalt, to taste2 tbsp olive oil1 loaf crusty breadBeat the eggs with a pinch of salt.Heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently for about 3 minutes until just set underneath and soft on top.Fold the omelette, slide it onto a plate and cut into four. Serve with the crusty bread torn into pieces.
